summary: Confirmed all three requested estimates against the PDF and the extraction rules/codebook. Read the complete 116133-character markdown conversion in consecutive chunks, including references and Appendices A-L. PDF p. 22, Table 2, prints Human-AI coefficients and standard errors of 0.327 (0.024) for text quality, -0.133 (0.021) for image quality, and -0.013 (0.021) for click likelihood, with 45803 rating observations in each analysis. The text and image coefficients have three stars, defined as p<0.001; no exact click p-value is printed. The demographic-only columns of Table G on PDF p. 51 reproduce these results. PDF p. 19 explicitly identifies ratings as the observation unit, while the notes to Tables 2 and G explicitly cluster standard errors by ad. Therefore unit=rating and se_basis=output are consistent: the uncertainty treats ads as independent and does not account for multiple ads from the same randomized creator. Analysis-specific creator counts are not printed, so n_treatment, n_control, and n_total appropriately remain null; the overall creator and separate evaluator counts cannot substitute for them. The question, construct, measure, higher_is, AI availability, timing, within-person status, arms, and active-comparator coding agree with the methods on PDF pp. 11, 14-15, and 17-20. Text and image quality are usefulness ratings; click likelihood is an other outcome with its direction explained. All three concern outputs created during the assisted session, with subsequent evaluation of those same outputs. No eligible outcome or contrast is missing under extraction rules 4-6: productivity, diversity, human and AI quality ratings, and copy-completion outcomes are represented. Additional work-process-adjusted quality models, mechanism/moderation analyses, and field models controlling for post-treatment ratings and/or campaign spend are excluded and listed in not_extracted. The review of other estimates was limited to completeness; this report verifies only the three requested estimates.
